\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{انهار} (inhāra)}{انهار (inhāra)}]{\ar{انهار} (inhāra) — to collapse}

\label{lesson:AR-C316-inhara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to defeat, then the Arabic for to surrender.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{انهار}}
\textbf{\ar{انهار}} — \emph{inhāra} — \textquotedblleft{}to collapse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انهار} \ar{البيت} \ar{القديم} \ar{بعد} \ar{المطر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{inhāra al-bayt al-qadīm baʿda al-maṭar.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The old house collapsed after the rain.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينهار}, \emph{yanhār}.

Of a person: \ar{انهار} \ar{بعد} \ar{الخبر}, he broke down at the news.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{انهار}} (\emph{inhāra}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{h-w-r} (Lane), said of a building or a bank of earth that falls down. It is Form VII, \textquotedblleft{}to tumble down\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inhāra}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inhāra}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inhāra al-bayt al-qadīm baʿda al-maṭar.} — The old house collapsed after the rain.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to defeat, then the Arabic for to surrender, then say \emph{inhāra} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{انهار} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To collapse\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{فاض} (fāḍa)}{فاض (fāḍa)}]{\ar{فاض} (fāḍa) — to overflow, to flood}

\label{lesson:AR-C316-fada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to surrender, then the Arabic for to collapse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{فاض}}
\textbf{\ar{فاض}} — \emph{fāḍa} — \textquotedblleft{}to overflow, to flood\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{فاض} \ar{النهر} \ar{بعد} \ar{الأمطار}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{fāḍa an-nahr baʿda al-amṭār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The river overflowed after the rains.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يفيض}, \emph{yafīḍ}.

The taught \ar{فيضان}, a flood, is its verbal noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{فاض}} (\emph{fāḍa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-y-ḍ} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to overflow, to run over\textquotedblright{}, the root of the taught \emph{fayaḍān}, a flood.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fāḍa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fāḍa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fāḍa an-nahr baʿda al-amṭār.} — The river overflowed after the rains.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to surrender, then the Arabic for to collapse, then say \emph{fāḍa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{فاض} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To overflow, to flood\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اندلع} (indalaʿa)}{اندلع (indalaʿa)}]{\ar{اندلع} (indalaʿa) — to break out}

\label{lesson:AR-C316-indalaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to collapse, then the Arabic for to overflow.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اندلع}}
\textbf{\ar{اندلع}} — \emph{indalaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to break out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اندلع} \ar{حريق} \ar{في} \ar{السوق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{indalaʿa ḥarīq fī as-sūq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A fire broke out in the market.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يندلع}, \emph{yandaliʿ}.

Of fires, wars and quarrels.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اندلع}} (\emph{indalaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-l-ʿ} (Lane), said of a tongue that lolls out and of a sword that slips from its sheath. It is Form VII; a fire or a war that breaks out comes from that sense.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{indalaʿa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{indalaʿa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{indalaʿa ḥarīq fī as-sūq.} — A fire broke out in the market.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to collapse, then the Arabic for to overflow, then say \emph{indalaʿa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{اندلع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To break out\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ركام} (rukām)}{ركام (rukām)}]{\ar{ركام} (rukām) — rubble, a heap}

\label{lesson:AR-C316-rukam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to overflow, then the Arabic for to break out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ركام}}
\textbf{\ar{ركام}} — \emph{rukām} — \textquotedblleft{}rubble, a heap\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{بحث} \ar{الناس} \ar{تحت} \ar{الركام} \ar{عن} \ar{الأطفال}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{baḥatha an-nās taḥta ar-rukām ʿan al-aṭfāl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
People searched under the rubble for the children.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ركام}} (\emph{rukām}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-k-m} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to pile one thing on another\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Rukām} is a heap, of clouds or of stones.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rukām}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rukām}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baḥatha an-nās taḥta ar-rukām ʿan al-aṭfāl.} — People searched under the rubble for the children.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to overflow, then the Arabic for to break out, then say \emph{rukām} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أنقاض} (anqāḍ)}{أنقاض (anqāḍ)}]{\ar{أنقاض} (anqāḍ) — ruins, debris}

\label{lesson:AR-C316-anqad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to break out, then the Arabic for rubble.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أنقاض}}
\textbf{\ar{أنقاض}} — \emph{anqāḍ} — \textquotedblleft{}ruins, debris\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{بني} \ar{بيت} \ar{جديد} \ar{فوق} \ar{أنقاض} \ar{البيت} \ar{القديم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{buniya bayt jadīd fawqa anqāḍ al-bayt al-qadīm.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A new house was built on the ruins of the old one.
\end{quote}

A plural word, as English ruins.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أنقاض}} (\emph{anqāḍ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-q-ḍ} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to undo, to pull down a building\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Anqāḍ} is the plural of \emph{niqḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}what has been pulled down\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{anqāḍ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{anqāḍ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{buniya bayt jadīd fawqa anqāḍ al-bayt al-qadīm.} — A new house was built on the ruins of the old one.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to break out, then the Arabic for rubble, then say \emph{anqāḍ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 309–316 — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R316-review-309-316}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for a prince and a palace.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a prince, a palace, a crown, a throne, to crown
  \item to call for help, to survive, to cry out, to call out to, a rescuer
  \item childbirth, a newborn, a midwife, to have a child, a naming
  \item to uncover, to discover, to come across, an explorer, a treasure
  \item on the spot, before long, gradually, anew, to regain
  \item a funeral, to pass away, to bury, to escort a coffin, a grave
  \item a victory in battle, a defeat, to win a victory, to defeat, to surrender
  \item to collapse, to overflow, to break out, rubble, ruins
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A prince? (\textbf{\ar{أمير}}, \emph{amīr}.) A palace? (\textbf{\ar{قصر}}, \emph{qaṣr}.) A crown? (\textbf{\ar{تاج}}, \emph{tāj}.) A throne? (\textbf{\ar{عرش}}, \emph{ʿarsh}.) To crown? (\textbf{\ar{توج}}, \emph{tawwaja}.) To call for help? (\textbf{\ar{استغاث}}, \emph{istaghātha}.) To survive? (\textbf{\ar{نجا}}, \emph{najā}.) To cry out? (\textbf{\ar{صاح}}, \emph{ṣāḥa}.) To call out to? (\textbf{\ar{نادى}}, \emph{nādā}.) A rescuer? (\textbf{\ar{منقذ}}, \emph{munqidh}.) Childbirth? (\textbf{\ar{ولادة}}, \emph{wilāda}.) A newborn? (\textbf{\ar{مولود}}, \emph{mawlūd}.) A midwife? (\textbf{\ar{قابلة}}, \emph{qābila}.) To have a child? (\textbf{\ar{أنجب}}, \emph{anjaba}.) A naming? (\textbf{\ar{تسمية}}, \emph{tasmiya}.) To uncover? (\textbf{\ar{كشف}}, \emph{kashafa}.) To discover? (\textbf{\ar{اكتشف}}, \emph{iktashafa}.) To come across? (\textbf{\ar{عثر}}, \emph{ʿathara}.) An explorer? (\textbf{\ar{مستكشف}}, \emph{mustakshif}.) A treasure? (\textbf{\ar{كنز}}, \emph{kanz}.) On the spot? (\textbf{\ar{على} \ar{الفور}}, \emph{ʿalā al-fawr}.) Before long? (\textbf{\ar{سرعان} \ar{ما}}, \emph{surʿāna mā}.) Gradually? (\textbf{\ar{تدريجيا}}, \emph{tadrījiyyan}.) Anew? (\textbf{\ar{من} \ar{جديد}}, \emph{min jadīd}.) To regain? (\textbf{\ar{استعاد}}, \emph{istaʿāda}.) A funeral? (\textbf{\ar{جنازة}}, \emph{janāza}.) To pass away? (\textbf{\ar{توفي}}, \emph{tuwuffiya}.) To bury? (\textbf{\ar{دفن}}, \emph{dafana}.) To escort a coffin? (\textbf{\ar{شيع}}, \emph{shayyaʿa}.) A grave? (\textbf{\ar{قبر}}, \emph{qabr}.) A victory in battle? (\textbf{\ar{نصر}}, \emph{naṣr}.) A defeat? (\textbf{\ar{هزيمة}}, \emph{hazīma}.) To win a victory? (\textbf{\ar{انتصر}}, \emph{intaṣara}.) To defeat? (\textbf{\ar{هزم}}, \emph{hazama}.) To surrender? (\textbf{\ar{استسلم}}, \emph{istaslama}.) To collapse? (\textbf{\ar{انهار}}, \emph{inhāra}.) To overflow? (\textbf{\ar{فاض}}, \emph{fāḍa}.) To break out? (\textbf{\ar{اندلع}}, \emph{indalaʿa}.) Rubble? (\textbf{\ar{ركام}}, \emph{rukām}.) Ruins? (\textbf{\ar{أنقاض}}, \emph{anqāḍ}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
